t: They are asleep already. I should stop moving before I wake them.
Their breathing is steady. Mine will be once I stop thinking.
We forgot to bank the fire again. I suppose it is my turn.
They left enough blanket for me tonight. I should mention that tomorrow.
The room is dark, but I know exactly where they left their boots.
They turned over when I came in and went straight back to sleep.
I can hear rain, the fire, and somebody I love snoring.
We should talk tomorrow. Neither of us has good sense this late.
Their side is warm. I will try not to shove them over.
I woke them coming through the door. They said nothing, which is worse.
They talk less in sleep than people claim, but much less clearly.
We are still annoyed with each other. Morning may make it smaller.
The roof creaked and both of us pretended not to hear it.
They reached for me without waking. That was enough.
We need to move the bed. Moonlight finds my face every night.
I should whisper an apology now or give a better one tomorrow.
They kicked the blanket away and will complain about the cold soon.
The house settles differently after dark. They sleep through every sound.
We made it through another day without fixing that draft.
They are waiting up for me. I can tell by the lamp.
I should lie down before they ask why I am pacing.
Their cold feet always find me after the fire dies.
The day feels less serious when we whisper about it in bed.
They remembered to latch the door. I can stop wondering now.
I like this quiet best when I am not alone in it.
They asked about my day, and I was too tired to answer properly.
We both came home exhausted and left the floor exactly as it was.
I should eat, wash, and speak. Sitting here is winning instead.
They saved me supper. I am almost too tired to lift the spoon.
We can leave the ashes until morning. Nobody will mind.
I snapped at them because my back hurt. That was not fair.
They know I am finished for the day by how slowly I remove my boots.
We planned to talk tonight. Sleep may have a stronger claim.
They rubbed my shoulders without asking what the work had done.
I should thank them before tiredness turns into silence.
Both of us are waiting for the other to tend the fire.
They started telling me something important. I nearly fell asleep halfway through.
I have enough strength left to reach the bed and nothing else.
We should stop pretending either of us will sweep tonight.
They look as tired as I feel. We should be gentle.
Supper is cold, the room is warm, and I do not mind.
I promised to listen. I need to keep my eyes open first.
They took one look at me and moved their things off the bed.
I am too tired to argue, which may improve the evening.
Tomorrow needs both of us rested more than tonight needs another chore.
The house sounds larger at night when every neighbor has gone quiet.
I should check the latch once, not every time the wind moves it.
The fire is low enough to leave until morning.
I can hear somebody walking outside. Their steps are unhurried.
The bed is cold now, but it will not stay that way.
I left water beside the bed and already forgot where.
A little moonlight comes through the roof where rain probably will too.
The floor creaks near the door and nowhere else.
I woke for no reason and now every small sound matters.
The room smells of yesterday's fire after dark.
I should close the window before the bedding turns damp.
The village is quiet enough that I can hear the roof settle.
I forgot to bring tomorrow's clothes near the bed.
The wind sounds worse from bed than it did outside.
One more log should last until the first light.
The patch above the hearth stayed dry through the last rain.
I should check the roof pegs before the wind returns.
A roof is mostly something you notice when it fails.
That dark mark on the beam was smaller yesterday.
The thatch needs pressing down along the far edge.
I heard one drip and spent the next hour looking for it.
The roof held, though the wind tried every corner.
I should replace the damp reeds before they soften the beam.
Sunlight through that gap means rain will find it too.
The ridge looks straight from inside. I should inspect it outside.
I am too tired to find another dry place tonight.
The ground feels harder after a full day on my feet.
I need sleep badly enough that the cold may not stop me.
There is no good place to lie down, only less wet ones.
My blanket is damp and I lack the strength to dry it.
I worked on other people's roofs and still sleep under the sky.
The fire is crowded. I will take whatever warmth reaches the edge.
I cannot remember the last night I woke truly rested.
Another cold night will make tomorrow's work harder again.
I would trade every proud thought for a dry bed.
The bandage catches on the bedding whenever I turn.
At least I can rest this leg somewhere dry.
The wound hurts more after I stop moving around.
I should wash the cut again before lying down.
The stool is exactly where my bruised knee keeps finding it.
I can hide a limp outside. The walk across this room still shows it.
The healer said to rest. The unfinished chores disagree.
Warm water takes the edge off the pain for a little while.
I should stop touching the bruise to see whether it still hurts.
Getting into bed was harder than admitting I needed help.
I still think of telling them things before remembering they are already gone.
They know which silence means anger and which one means tiredness.
I should ask about their day before explaining mine.
We need time together that is not borrowed from work.
They remembered something I said once and forgot immediately.
I know when they are worried because they start fixing harmless things.
We have changed each other's habits without ever discussing it.
They make bad days easier without pretending the days were good.
I owe them a patient answer when we speak tonight.
We should do something together that produces absolutely nothing useful.
